question_text: According to the course material, Ingalsbe and Groves (1989) group factors shaping cooperative development into three main types: economic conditions, farmer organizations, and:
explanation: The three interrelated types are economic conditions, farmer organizations and public policy.

question_text: According to the course material, colonial co-operative development in British colonies was channelled through specially created Departments of Co-operation or Co-operative Branches within their:
explanation: Colonial co-ops were channelled through Agriculture departments or Co-operation departments.

question_text: According to the course material, agricultural co-operatives in Ireland were spearheaded by Sir Horace Plunkett (1854-1932) and included the Irish Agricultural Organisation Society established in:
explanation: The Irish Agricultural Organisation Society was established in 1894.

question_text: According to the course material, in 1919 Plunkett created the Plunkett Foundation which became an international organisation for the promotion of:
explanation: The Plunkett Foundation (1919) promotes agricultural co-operatives.

question_text: According to the course material, Sir Daniel Hall explained that British agricultural co-operatives developed less strongly because the typical British farmer is a capitalist upon a comparatively large scale, not a:
explanation: British farmers were comparatively large-scale, not family-unit farmers.

question_text: According to the course material, government first Co-operative legislation, the Co-operative Credit Societies Act, India, was passed in:
explanation: India's Co-operative Credit Societies Act was passed in 1904.

question_text: According to the course material, about 90% of all farming soil in Denmark was cooperative from 1300, as the Black Death depopulated rural parts; inhabitants of a Danish village would work together, forming:
explanation: Danish village communes were called Landsby faellesskaber.

question_text: According to the course material, the combination of the Cooperative Movement and the switch away from grain production resulted in Danish Bacon and:
explanation: The movement created Danish Bacon and Lurpak Butter brands.

question_text: According to the course material, Danish cooperatives were governed democratically, usually each member had one vote irrespective of the number of cows he possessed; in the 1950s dairies united into Mejeriselskaberne Danmark and Klover who later merged to found MD Foods, now:
explanation: MD Foods is now Arla Foods and controls almost all of the Danish milk market.

question_text: According to the course material, the first cooperative abattoir in Denmark was formed in 1887; the Danish Crown meat processing company also owes its existence to the:
explanation: Danish Crown owes its existence to the cooperative movement; first abattoir 1887.

question_text: According to the course material, Danish co-op stores known as Brugsen were under the administration of The Danish Consumers Co-operative Society; in January 2002 Coop shops merged with retail chains from:
explanation: In January 2002 Coop shops merged with Coop Norden.

question_text: According to the course material, the cooperative ownership model for wind mills was developed in Denmark; one of the biggest cooperatively owned windfarms is at Middelgrunden in Copenhagen and at:
explanation: Middelgrunden in Copenhagen and Samsø island are major cooperative windfarms.

question_text: According to the course material, Charles Gide distinguished consumer co-operatives from collectivist expropriation: the essential article of the Socialist programme, class conflict, cannot be included in the co-operative programme because the consumer does not represent any:
explanation: Gide: the consumer does not represent any class; everybody is a consumer.

question_text: According to the course material, British consumer co-operation received no government support or sanction and operated within the nation's:
explanation: British consumer co-ops received no government support and operated within the tax regime.

question_text: According to the course material, factors that led to success of consumers cooperative movement in Britain included the Plunkett Foundation (1919), communications networks of the British Empire, registration including promotion supervision and auditing, establishment of a national credit bank, increased use of highly technical personnel as managers, and increased use of:
explanation: Success factors include auxiliary departments for auditing, traffic, education, testing and marketing research.

question_text: According to the course material, in 1752 Benjamin Franklin became perhaps the first American cooperator with the organization of a mutual insurance cooperative called the Philadelphia Contributionship for the Insurance of Houses from:
explanation: Franklin organised the Philadelphia Contributionship for insurance from loss by fire.

question_text: According to the course material, in 1803 the first formal farmers' marketing cooperative was organized in:
explanation: The first formal farmers' marketing cooperative was organised in Ohio in 1803.

question_text: According to the course material, about 1810 two dairy cooperatives thought to be the first formal farmers' associations in the United States were located at Goshen, Connecticut, and:
explanation: The two 1810 dairy coops were at Goshen, Connecticut and South Trenton, New Jersey.

question_text: According to the course material, by 1890 there were about 1,000 active farmer cooperatives in the United States; over 700 of these were handling:
explanation: Over 700 of about 1,000 farmer cooperatives handled dairy products.

question_text: According to the course material, Alphonse Desjardins of Quebec helped organize the first credit union in the United States; Massachusetts passed the first credit union act in:
explanation: Massachusetts passed the first credit union act in 1909.

question_text: According to the course material, with Franklin Roosevelt and the New Deal in 1933, the Rural Electrification Act was passed in 1936 to aid rural areas in obtaining electricity cooperatively, and a federal credit union act permitted:
explanation: The federal credit union act permitted Federal Chartering of credit unions.

question_text: According to the course material, since about 1988 two phenomena have been occurring in US agricultural cooperatives: restructuring and consolidation of conventional cooperatives, and the emergence of new generation cooperatives (NGCs) which focus on:
explanation: NGCs focus on value-added activities with closed or restricted membership.

question_text: According to the course material, Cook (1995) presents five core problems of conventional cooperatives: the free rider, horizon, portfolio, control, and:
explanation: Cook's five problems: free rider, horizon, portfolio, control, and influence cost.

question_text: According to the course material, the horizon problem arises when a member's residual claim on the net income generated by an asset is shorter than the:
explanation: Horizon problem: residual claim shorter than the asset's productive life.

question_text: According to the course material, the free-rider problem emerges when property rights are untradable, insecure, or unassigned; in a traditional cooperative rights to residual claims are linked to patronage instead of:
explanation: Residual claims are linked to patronage instead of investment, encouraging free riding.

question_text: According to the course material, there are some 26,000 agricultural cooperatives of all types in the United States, consisting of agricultural bargaining, credit, marketing, service, supply, fire mutual, fishery and:
explanation: Types include bargaining, credit, marketing, service, supply, fire mutual, fishery and Indian cooperatives.

question_text: According to the course material, the American Agricultural Marketing Association (AAMA) was incorporated in January 1960 under the Illinois Cooperative law as the national coordinating and information agency for some:
explanation: AAMA serves some 45 State Farm Bureau marketing associations.

question_text: According to the course material, the first person to introduce Co-operative Societies to India was Lord Wenlock; in 1892 he sent Mr. Frederick Nicholson to observe and study co-operation in Europe; Nicholson's report in 1901 led to the formation of many:
option_a: Co-operatives thrift and credit Societies amongst the farmers
explanation: Nicholson's 1901 report led to thrift and credit societies among farmers.

question_text: According to the course material, under the Montague-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919, cooperation became a provincial subject; under the Constitution of India the item Cooperative Societies is a State Subject under entry No.32 of the:
explanation: Cooperative Societies is a State Subject under entry No.32 of the State List.

question_text: According to the course material, a salient feature of the Indian cooperatives movement was the development of multipurpose cooperatives since 1937, strongly advocated by the:
explanation: Since 1937 the Reserve Bank of India has strongly advocated multipurpose cooperatives.

question_text: According to the course material, the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 1984 was enacted by Parliament under Entry No. 44 of the:
option_a: Union List of the Constitution of India
explanation: The 1984 Act was enacted under Entry No. 44 of the Union List.

question_text: According to the course material, the All-India Rural Credit Survey Committee Report of 1954 recommended an integrated approach to cooperative credit and emphasised viable credit cooperative societies by expanding their area of operation, encouraging rural savings and diversifying business; it also recommended Government participation in the:
explanation: The 1954 report recommended government participation in cooperative share capital.
